name: Courtroom / Legal Drama
definition: Competing advocates transform disputed facts into persuasive narratives under procedural rules, unequal resources, and consequences that extend beyond the verdict.
diagnostic_questions: Do competing accounts of the same facts drive the conflict?
Do procedure and proof materially constrain what characters can accomplish?

neighbors.distinction: A trial contests provable accounts; a mystery primarily reconstructs a hidden event.
Legal drama focuses conflict through institutions of proof and judgment.

reader_promises.name: Competing cases
reader_promises.description: Give opposing narratives credible evidence, omissions, and human consequences.

reader_promises.name: Earned judgment
reader_promises.description: Make the decisive outcome follow from developed proof, strategy, and character choice.

roles.name: Advocate
roles.description: Builds a case while balancing truth, duty, strategy, and personal investment.

roles.name: Witness
roles.description: Supplies evidence filtered through memory, loyalty, fear, or limited perspective.

roles.name: Adjudicator
roles.description: Embodies the rules and interpretive limits governing the decision.

movements.name: Case framed
movements.description: Define the legal question, burdens, parties, and personal consequences.

movements.name: Narratives built
movements.description: Develop rival accounts through preparation, witnesses, and evidence.

movements.name: Proof tested
movements.description: Expose contradiction, bias, missing context, or a strategic weakness under pressure.

movements.name: Judgment and consequence
movements.description: Deliver a decision and reveal what formal judgment can and cannot resolve.

complications.name: Excluded proof
complications.description: Important information cannot be used in the obvious way.

complications.name: Client conflict
complications.description: The represented person's goal diverges from the advocate's strategy or ethics.

complications.name: Public pressure
complications.description: Media, politics, or community fear alters participants without replacing legal causality.

twists.name: Context shift
twists.description: Known evidence gains a different legal or moral meaning under fuller context.

twists.name: Remedy cost
twists.description: Winning the case requires a remedy that harms a value the victor sought to protect.

conclusions.name: Just verdict
conclusions.description: The process reaches a defensible result through earned advocacy and proof.

conclusions.name: Legal and moral split
conclusions.description: The lawful outcome diverges from the story's fuller moral truth.

conclusions.name: Systemic consequence
conclusions.description: The case changes a rule, institution, or public understanding beyond the parties.

variation_axes.question: What kind of resolution is possible?

subversions: Let careful preparation defeat the surprise-witness cliché.
Make listening and reframing more decisive than theatrical aggression.
cliches_to_avoid: A last-minute confession unsupported by prior pressure
Procedure that changes only when the plot needs it
quality_checks: Both sides organize evidence into intelligible competing accounts.
Rules create choices and costs rather than decorative jargon.
The aftermath distinguishes verdict from truth and healing.

sources.title: Narrative, Truth, and Trial
sources.contribution: Examines how adjudicators organize testimony into competing narratives and where that model fails.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Popular Fiction
sources.contribution: Supports treating popular genres as flexible repertoires of narrative pleasure.
